alerts.title: TDF nephrotoxicity risk: proteinuria and NSAID use with hypertension
alerts.message: Guidelines advise TDF be avoided if eGFR < 50 mL/min/1.73m2 and call for close renal monitoring in high-risk patients, particularly those with co-existent hypertension. Today creatinine is 112 umol/L with trace proteinuria and BP 146/94 mmHg, while the patient takes ibuprofen as needed on top of TDF. The clinician attributes proteinuria to hypertension, but TDF nephrotoxicity and NSAID-related renal injury are not excluded; the creatinine is not yet a documented eGFR and no creatinine trend is available to confirm stability. Ibuprofen plus TDF with hypertension compounds renal risk.

evidence.recommended_action: Calculate eGFR now and repeat creatinine/eGFR and urinalysis at 3 months. Counsel to avoid ibuprofen; consider non-NSAID analgesia. Monitor closely for renal toxicity and review TDF suitability if eGFR falls below 50.

alerts.title: Low serum phosphate with TDF: possible proximal tubulopathy
alerts.message: Guidelines list tubular wasting syndrome as a common or severe adverse effect of TDF, and recommend renal monitoring including after intercurrent illness. Serum phosphate today is 0.78 mmol/L, low, alongside trace proteinuria and thigh heaviness with lumbar tenderness, consistent with possible Fanconi-type tubulopathy and bone involvement. Alternative causes such as poor intake or hypertension are not excluded, and phosphate was not previously monitored, so no trend is available.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat serum phosphate, urine studies and eGFR promptly. Evaluate for tenofovir-associated tubulopathy and bone demineralisation; if confirmed, discuss switching TDF to TAF per guideline.

alerts.title: Amlodipine nonadherence and BP control in a high-risk patient
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend that hypertension medicines be managed with attention to side effects and adherence, and that TDF-treated patients with hypertension are high risk for renal harm. BP is 146/94 mmHg with admitted missed amlodipine doses during transit. Lower limb oedema is absent today, so amlodipine side effects are not currently driving nonadherence; the barrier appears to be travel-related.

evidence.recommended_action: Address adherence barriers related to travel (dose timing, supply, reminders). Recheck BP and monitor for amlodipine side effects such as oedema; consider alternatives if these develop.
